note: Fishing on the San Pedro Channel: what lives where, what it takes, how big it runs and what may be kept. All of it is from general knowledge of Southern California sport fishing, not from a survey or the current regulations booklet: sizes, limits and positions are approximate. No-take reserves are not listed here, nor the oil platforms and islands: both come from this water's features.json (its `noTake` areas through fishing/zones.ts, its `structures` through fishing/table.ts), so there is one list of each. Read by apps/client/src/fishing/table.ts; the rules that use it are in fishing/grounds.ts and fishing/bites.ts. Lengths in centimetres, positions in flat metres east and north of the course origin.
name: Southern California

grounds.name: Alamitos Bay
grounds.say: Spotted bay bass round the docks and the eelgrass, halibut on the sand in the entrance.

grounds.name: the bait barge
grounds.say: Stop here for a scoop of live sardines.

grounds.name: the harbor flats
grounds.say: Sand inside the breakwater: halibut on a drifted bait, sand bass and croaker.

grounds.name: the San Pedro breakwater
grounds.say: Calico and sand bass tight to the rocks.

grounds.name: the middle breakwater
grounds.say: Calico and sand bass tight to the rocks, bonito off the ends.

grounds.name: the Long Beach breakwater
grounds.say: Calico and sand bass tight to the rocks, bonito off the ends.

grounds.name: Horseshoe Kelp
grounds.say: A low reef three miles out: sand bass, calico, sculpin, and barracuda over the top of it.

grounds.name: the island kelp line
grounds.say: The kelp along the island's front side: calico, sheephead, whitefish, and white seabass at first light.

grounds.name: Hen Rock
grounds.say: The reef just outside the Long Point reserve: yellowtail come round the corner along the kelp.

grounds.name: the East End
grounds.say: Yellowtail off the corner of the island, and the first place a marlin is seen.

grounds.name: Bird Rock
grounds.say: A white rock off the Isthmus with yellowtail and calico round it.

grounds.name: Ship Rock
grounds.say: A pinnacle in deep water: yellowtail and bonito on top, whitefish down the sides.

grounds.name: Catalina Harbor
grounds.say: Mud and sand on the back side: halibut and bass.

grounds.name: White's Landing
grounds.say: A long sand beach: halibut on the flat off it.

grounds.name: the far side of the channel
grounds.say: Blue water under the island: the tuna and the marlin, when they are in.

species.name: calico bass
species.limit: 14 inches to keep, five bass a day
species.hint: Calico live in the kelp and on the rocks and platform legs. A live sardine at the edge of the kelp is the way.

species.name: sand bass
species.limit: 14 inches to keep, five bass a day
species.hint: Sand bass sit on low reef and hard sand in 10 to 40 m and bite into the evening.

species.name: spotted bay bass
species.limit: 14 inches to keep, so nearly all of them go back
species.hint: Spotted bay bass live inside the bay round docks and eelgrass, and bite best on a moving tide.

species.name: California halibut
species.limit: 22 inches to keep, five a day
species.hint: Halibut lie on sand in 3 to 20 m and want a live bait drifted slowly over them on a moving tide.

species.name: yellowfin croaker
species.limit: no size limit, ten a day
species.hint: Croaker feed on the shallow sand, best early, late and after dark, on a bit of squid.

species.name: Pacific mackerel
species.limit: no limit
species.hint: Mackerel are everywhere there is bait, and take anything small.

species.name: Pacific bonito
species.limit: ten a day
species.hint: Bonito chase bait outside the gate and round the platforms. Troll feathers at 5 to 7 kt or cast to the birds.

species.name: Pacific barracuda
species.limit: 28 inches to keep, ten a day
species.hint: Barracuda run over the reefs and along the kelp in summer. Feathers at 5 to 7 kt, or an iron.

species.name: yellowtail
species.limit: 24 inches to keep, ten a day
species.hint: Yellowtail hold off the island's points, round the platforms and under kelp paddies. A live bait, or a plug at 6 to 8 kt.

species.name: dorado
species.limit: no size limit, ten a day
species.hint: Dorado come up the coast in warm water and live under floating kelp paddies. Find a paddy, stop short of it and cast, or troll past its edge at 7 to 9 kt.

species.name: skipjack tuna
species.limit: ten a day
species.hint: Skipjack run with the warm water in the open channel and take small lures trolled fast.

species.name: yellowfin tuna
species.limit: ten tuna a day
species.hint: Yellowfin show as foamers: white water and diving birds on the far side of the channel. Get ahead of them, stop, and cast, or troll a plug past the edge at 7 to 9 kt.

species.name: bluefin tuna
species.limit: two a day
species.hint: Bluefin are the trip-maker: foamers at dawn and dusk on the far side. They are line-shy and they do not stop.

species.name: striped marlin
species.limit: one a day, and most are let go
species.measure: from the jaw to the fork
species.hint: A striped marlin is a late-summer fish of the far side and the East End: a big lure at 7 to 9 kt, and a lot of empty miles.

species.name: sheephead
species.limit: 12 inches to keep, two a day
species.hint: Sheephead crunch mussels off the rocks and the platform legs by day. Squid on the bottom.

species.name: ocean whitefish
species.limit: ten a day
species.hint: Whitefish are on the island's rocky bottom outside the kelp, in 20 m and more, on squid.

species.name: white seabass
species.limit: 28 inches to keep, three a day
species.hint: White seabass ghost along the kelp at grey light and are gone when the sun is on the water. Be on the kelp line before dawn with a live bait.

species.name: opaleye
species.limit: ten a day
species.hint: Opaleye graze the shallow rocks and take a small bait by day.

species.name: rockfish
species.limit: ten a day in all
species.hint: Rockfish stack up deep under the platforms, in 45 m and more. Squid or a heavy iron on the bottom.

species.name: sculpin
species.limit: 10 inches to keep, five a day, and mind the spines
species.hint: Sculpin sit on hard bottom in 20 m and more and bite best in the evening and after dark.

species.name: giant sea bass
species.protected: Giant sea bass are protected and none may be kept: let her go at the rail
species.limit: protected: always let go
species.hint: Giant sea bass, as long as a man, live in the kelp and under the platforms. They are protected: a fish to meet, not to keep.
